title: Add RAG assertion factory and local eval runner for lightweight acceptance tests
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: teams building RAG integrations often need a small, deterministic harness to assert retrieval and generation behavior against a fixed prompt set. This PR adds a compact 'assertion factory' quickstart that: 1) provides a collection of typed assertion templates for common RAG checks (presence, factuality, citation-to-source, and structured-schema validation), 2) ships a tiny local eval-runner that executes assertions against live or recorded model responses, and 3) integrates lightweight telemetry probes to make regression diagnostics actionable.

What changed (high level):
- New quickstart under quickstarts/rag-assertion-factory with README, step scripts, and examples.
- A small Node-based runner (bin/local-eval-runner.js) that can run assertion sets against a Redwood hosted API key or a recorded session (fixtures/).
- Typed assertion templates and example contract files (templates/), with schema examples for structured output checks.
- CI smoke job and a local dev script to generate a golden fixture for offline runs.

Checklist:
- [x] Quickstart README with step-by-step getting started and common troubleshooting notes.
- [x] Example assertion templates and sample fixtures.
- [x] Local runner with --record and --replay modes.
- [x] CI job that runs the runner in replay mode on commit.
- [x] Telemetry hooks added to surface failed assertions in traces.

Related work: ENG-4231 (RAG regression tooling), ENG-4287 (telemetry probes for quickstarts). See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/rag-assertion-factory for the staged doc landing page.

Notes on design: the assertion DSL intentionally remains small and composable: checks are expressed as JSON objects with a type (contains/exact-match/schema/citation) and threshold fields. The runner performs deterministic normalization (whitespace, punctuation, unicode NFKC) before checks so fixtures are stable across model minor versions. Recorded fixtures are gzip-compressed JSONL to keep CI fast.

Upgrade notes: this quickstart is additive and opt-in; it does not change runtime behavior or SDKs. If teams later adopt the assertion templates, we recommend adding a replay-based smoke check to their PR pipelines.

release_notes: Add compact RAG assertion factory quickstart: provides assertion templates, a local eval-runner, example fixtures, and a CI smoke job for replay-based acceptance checks. Useful for teams adding automated RAG regression tests.
notes_on_ci: Initial CI run failed due to missing gzip binary in the container; workflow updated to install 'gzip' in runner image. Final CI run passed (smoke replay).
usage_examples:
1) Record: node bin/local-eval-runner.js --record --api-key=$REDWOOD_KEY --out=fixtures/my-session.jsonl.gz
2) Replay: node bin/local-eval-runner.js --replay=fixtures/my-session.jsonl.gz --assert=templates/assertion-presets.json
dev_tip: When authoring assertion templates, prefer small focused checks (one assertion per expected behavior). Use '--rebase-fixture' to update golden fixtures and commit only after review.
